risk_register: Persistence boundary risk: implementing direct app-api writes or a new local OLTP store could violate the Redis/historical-store architecture decision.
Promotion safety risk: validation or backtest success could be mistaken for approval; promotion must require explicit operator action.
Compiler semantic risk: SignalSpec transforms may compile to FeatureNode graphs that differ from validator assumptions unless references, cycles, and graph invariants are checked consistently.
Backtest duplication risk: introducing a SignalSpec-only replay path could diverge from R-015 deterministic results.
Diagnostics quality risk: validator failures may be correct but not actionable enough for LLM-authored repair loops.
Concurrency risk: simultaneous promote/archive or version replacement can create stale lifecycle state without version-checked transitions.
Durability and invariant risk: YAML body, compiled graph identity, signalVersion, and trackRecord can diverge or be partially accepted after failure unless promotion verifies persisted invariants.
Provenance drift risk: API opportunity envelopes or UI views may omit author, proposalId, signalVersion, or trackRecord even if catalog data is complete.
Runtime risk: promoted SignalSpecs may affect ranking latency or allocation behavior if compiled nodes bypass existing primitives.
Security risk: author/proposal fields and YAML diagnostics must be rendered safely and must not enable path access or arbitrary code execution.
